mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns in such regimes are not statistically different from a zero return (p > 0.05) in a 5-year walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver positive 20-day forward returns as market anticipates rate cuts within the next quarter.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 40 instances where the trigger occurred, 20-day forward returns were negative or flat (cumulative IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a tight labor market, which pushes equity valuations higher and drives positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over 10 out of 20 test windows with the trigger, 5-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 2% for two consecutive months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as it indicates weakening demand for capital assets.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >=2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 out of 30 instances of the trigger, forward returns are not meaningfully negative (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the INDPRO (industrial production) index falls by more than 5% from the prior month, it reflects supply-side weakness that elevates risk premia and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 40% of triggered periods, 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.25).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) over four consecutive months suggests a shift toward a liquidity trap, which tends to flatten the S&P 500 20-day forward return profile.
failure_condition: In 50% of such periods, 20-day forward returns are not positive (IC < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (labor) with UNRATE below 4% indicates a resilient labor market and expanding housing demand, both of which are associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% and PAYEMS increases by >8% while UNRATE < 4%
regime_hint: labor market resilience and housing recovery
failure_condition: In 8 out of 20 windows with the trigger, 5-day returns are not positive (IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL's 6-month change is negative, the S&P 500 is expected to post positive 20-day forward returns regardless of the underlying domain (trend or regime-specific).
failure_condition: In 30% of such triggers, 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
